feedback_signal: After the inactive DashboardView review graph was removed, adversarial review found that ReviewPresentation and its tests remained even though no production source constructs or consumes that model.
root_operational_failure: The first legacy-cleanup boundary enumerated private view roots but did not trace model and test-only dependencies to a fixed point, allowing an obsolete production model to remain after its last production consumer was removed.

durable_improvement.action: Add a focused source-contract assertion that the retired ReviewPresentation model and its legacy-only ReviewPopoverTests constructions are absent after the explicitly scoped cleanup.
durable_improvement.prevents: Future legacy-view deletions from leaving a production model and test cluster with no active caller.

commands.evidence: Before cleanup, testRetiredReviewPresentationIsAbsentFromModelAndLegacyTests failed its two absence assertions because ReviewPresentation remained in DashboardModels.swift and ReviewPopoverTests.swift. This was the expected red state.

After cleanup, SkillContractTests executed 4 tests with 0 failures. The focused target compiled DashboardModels.swift, the retained ReviewPopoverTests.swift test target, and ReleaseEvidenceView.swift without restoring a ReviewPresentation reference.

proof.future_behavior: A private UI graph removal that retires its last production model consumer must either retain an explicit supported caller or remove the model and its legacy-only tests under a focused source-contract guard.

implementation_note: This is a separate approved cleanup slice limited to DashboardModels.swift, ReviewPopoverTests.swift, the focused contract test, and governed evidence artifacts. It must not touch staged ReleaseEvidenceView.swift or the retained visual baseline.
